newsitem.title: USA: Excel on target for 15 pct sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Excel on target for 15 pct sales growth.

text.p: Excel Industries Inc said Friday it is on target for its ongoing goal of 15 percent sales growth while boosting earnings.
Excel said in a statement that it expects the company will continue to reach its "long-term sales growth target of 15 percent with good earnings progress".
Excel, which makes windows, doors and seats for cars and light trucks, on Thursday said first-quarter earnings rose to $0.59 a share on a primary basis from $0.46 in the same period of 1996.
Revenues beat the growth goal in the first quarter, rising nearly 67 percent to $251.22 million from $150.61 million, in part as a result of its Atwood acquisition, the company said.
"Our three major strategies remain intact -- growth by complementary acquisition, increasing globalization and continuous improvement," chief executive James Futterknecht, said in a statement.
The company said its Atwood automotive business, which lost money in 1996, was profitable in the first quarter.

North American light-vehicle production rose, but volume for Ford Motor Co, its largest customer, showed no increase as output of Ford's Taurus, Aerostar, Explorer and F-series pickups declined, Excel said.
Excel said its General Motors Corp programs recorded solid gains.
Shares of Excel were down 1/4 at 18-7/8.
